title: Personal Digital-Twin Data Freshness
dataSources: Daily life scores (`lifescore:daily`), personal SLO status (`personalslo:status`), cross-signal correlations (`correlation:pair`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The meta layer — correlating every `index=personal` feed (sleep, activity, mood, weather, spend, productivity, home telemetry) into daily life scores, personal SLOs, and cross-signal anomaly detection, all computed in Splunk.
spl:
index=personal
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen by sourcetype
| eval hours_silent=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1), stale=if(hours_silent>48,1,0)
| where stale=1
| sort - hours_silent
description: Checks every feed powering your personal digital twin is still reporting, catching a broken integration.
value: A digital twin is only as good as its data; a freshness sweep across all sourcetypes keeps the whole picture trustworthy.
implementation: Track last-seen per sourcetype across `index=personal`; alert on any feed that has gone quiet.
visualization: Table of personal feeds with time since last data.
grandmaExplanation: It checks every source of your life data is still updating, so nothing quietly stops feeding in.
